requirement: Page events newest first with a keyset cursor of creation time and id, so rows sharing a timestamp are neither skipped nor repeated, fetching one extra row to decide whether a next cursor exists, and bounding the page size.
skeleton: Base and an Event model with id, name and indexed created, a Cursor alias, and page_after validating size, ordering by created and id descending, filtering with a row-value comparison, and fetching size plus one.
caption: Keyset pagination with SQLAlchemy 2.0. Event is a declarative model with an integer id, a name and an indexed created datetime. page_after(session, cursor, size) raises ValueError saying size must be between 1 and 100 outside that range, builds a select ordered by created descending then id descending so ties have a deterministic order, and when a cursor is given adds a where clause comparing tuple_(Event.created, Event.id) against a tuple_ of the cursor values wrapped in literal with less-than, which continues exactly after the last row even inside a run of equal timestamps. It runs session.scalars with limit size plus one; if no extra row came back it returns the page and None, otherwise the page and a new cursor of the last row's created and id. The fixture builds seven events in an in-memory SQLite database where three share a timestamp, and asserts that the first page of three is e7, e6, e5 with cursor pointing at id 5, that walking pages of two visits every event exactly once in order, that a page of exactly all rows or more returns no cursor, and that sizes 0 and 101 raise ValueError.

plan.intent: Scroll through a large event table without offset scans
constraints: Order is created descending, then id descending
The cursor comparison uses both columns so ties are not skipped or repeated
The next cursor is None exactly when no further rows exist

rationale.teaches: Row-value comparison with tuple_ against a composite cursor, a matching composite order_by, and the limit plus one probe.
rationale.why: Filtering on the timestamp alone, using less-or-equal, or omitting the tiebreaker only breaks when timestamps collide at a page edge, so the fixture seeds a tie that straddles pages.

ops.docstring: Newest-first keyset pagination that stays stable when timestamps tie.

candidates.why_wrong: The cursor compares only the timestamp, so rows sharing it with the last row are skipped.
Less-or-equal repeats the last row of each page at the top of the next.
The cursor is taken from the extra probe row, so that row is skipped on the next page.
Fetching exactly size rows can never detect more data, so no next cursor is ever returned.
A page size of zero is accepted instead of raising ValueError.
